correctness.rationale: Every fixed-size probability is an exact coefficient ratio. Independent geometric and Bernoulli components realize the uniform overpartition after size conditioning. Forcing odd sizes replaces their Bernoulli bits by deterministic ones; the size mean changes O(t^-1) against standard deviation Θ(t^-3/2). A geometric-product Fourier bound supplies uniform lattice local limits and an all-m upper bound. The presence probability has log -t m²/2+o(1), with t~π/(2√n); the ratio tends to 1. The global Gaussian tail majorant establishes all real-positive moment convergence by dominated convergence. Exact integer DP verifies 2394 numerator identities, but no finite tests substitute for the limiting proof.

value.rationale: The first absent odd part is a natural and explicitly distinguished overpartition gap statistic in contemporary mex research. Its full limiting distribution and all real moments answer the natural frequency-scale question, with sharp constants including variance; the result is not a table recomputation or modular congruence and is substantially more informative than available first-sum results. Conditioning is nontrivial, addressed by an explicit all-m local Fourier bound.
